title: Orbit Forge
mechanics: A hands-on rocket-design and launch simulator. Configure body, fins, stages, nozzles, fuel tanks, and flight plan; the analysis panel reports launch mass, thrust-to-weight, drag, delta-v, stability, and projected burns.

actions: Skipped the Academy intro to open the hangar.
Selected the Heavy Lifter (3-stage) preset; the displayed design changed from 43.7 t / 5,173 m/s delta-v / 1.90 TWR to 107.7 t / 7,062 m/s / 1.80 TWR.
Selected Aggressive Turn and clicked LAUNCH; the live flight view entered a T−2 countdown with telemetry and all three stages visible.
gameplay.outcome: Rocket-design choices visibly changed mass, stage configuration, thrust-to-weight and delta-v; launch entered countdown. This confirms a physical-system simulation with consequential planning choices.
gameplay.limitations: The short check stopped during the countdown; no liftoff, orbit insertion, or landing was observed.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: The live hangar exposes rocket part/stage/fuel/flight-plan controls and performance analysis. The selected Heavy Lifter preset changed reported mass, TWR, and delta-v; LAUNCH entered a countdown.
A prior tester loaded the hangar, launched the default rocket, and observed altitude, speed, and fuel changing.

rationale: Simulators is primary because the game models rocket construction and flight physics. Strategy is a meaningful secondary category: choosing stages, engines, fuel, and a flight profile trades mass, thrust, drag, stability, and delta-v.

title: PES 6
mechanics: A browser port of Pro Evolution Soccer 6 for PSP. The current page presents commentary/language launch options and an Online tab with room controls, player-count selection (2–16), and public/private room settings.

actions: Opened the direct game page and allowed one short load interval; the engine/download panel then exposed commentary launch choices and the game settings UI.
gameplay.outcome: The page identifies a football game port and exposes match-launch and online-room UI, but no match, lobby, or human-versus-human result was observed in this pass.
gameplay.limitations: The embedded match did not start during the bounded check. Multiplayer is supported by the current Online room UI, but no room was entered and no players were observed.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: The live page identifies Pro Evolution Soccer 6 (PSP), offers commentary launch choices, and exposes an Online tab plus disabled public/private room controls for 2–16 players while the game is still at startup.

rationale: Sports is the core game: association football under PES rules. Multiplayer is supported by the port's explicit Online tab and public/private room controls with a human-player count; the review did not join a room.

title: Pocket Gridiron
mechanics: A football management and exhibition simulator using Pokémon teams, ratings, lineups, offensive styles, and fourth-down choices. Exhibition and season play generate full match scores and play-by-play; scouting and lineup editing are also available.

actions: Opened the exhibition dashboard, which showed a completed Kanto–Paldea football match and play-by-play.
Changed the home team's play style from Balanced to Run first; the page then displayed a different completed exhibition result (Kanto 24–Paldea 13 rather than the initially displayed 21–39).
gameplay.outcome: The page rendered football score/quarter totals, field position, and play-by-play; after the play-style choice the displayed simulation result changed. No player-controlled field movement was observed.
gameplay.limitations: No manual play execution, season progression, or individual lineup edit was tested in this pass.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: Current exhibition UI exposes team selection, Balanced/Run first/Air raid play styles, fourth-down choices, lineup editing, and a full scoreboard/play-by-play simulation. The visible result changed after selecting Run first.
A prior tester clicked KICK OFF and observed the scoreboard, quarter totals, weather, ball position, and play-by-play update.

rationale: Sports is primary because the simulated matches follow football rules. Strategy is secondary because lineups, offensive style, fourth-down decisions, season play, and scouting are central player choices; AI-simulated teams do not justify Multiplayer.

title: Puni Jump
mechanics: A portrait, score-based jump game: direct a mushroom character through short vertical stages, stomp spiky enemies, chain jumps for rising combo scores, and wall-jump. The current page's instructions show three lives and a 30-second opening stage.

actions: Opened the game splash through Tap to continue and selected the visible start control.
The game displayed Stage 01 with three hearts, a 30-second timer, and a jumping-tips overlay; pressed ArrowLeft once while that overlay remained open.
gameplay.outcome: Current UI explicitly describes left/right jumping, stomping, combo scoring, and wall-jumps. The tutorial remained open after the key press, so no current movement result was confirmed; a prior gameplay receipt recorded the avatar moving after input.
gameplay.limitations: No current stomp, score, or life change was observed. The prior dated test is kept separate from this pass.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: The current tutorial states left/right jump, stomp-from-above, combo-jump, and wall-jump rules; the opening HUD shows Stage 01, three lives, and 30 seconds.
A prior test entered Stage 01, pressed Left, observed the mushroom move and the game display NICE SLIP!, and documented the stomp/wall-jump controls.

rationale: Arcade fits the short timed stages, lives, score, and jump combos; Action fits active dodging and stomping. Platform traversal and wall-jumping are the defining genre and are not named by the existing categories, so Platformer is proposed as a shared new category.

title: Rage
mechanics: A first-person/over-the-shoulder corridor action game with a red energy blade. The page lists walking/turning, block, swing, blade throw, and grip/interact controls; the objective marker and health/grip/throw HUD indicate a combat encounter ahead.

actions: Clicked the game canvas and pressed Space at the title; the current page advanced to the 3D corridor scene.
Pressed Space at the ignite prompt and held ArrowUp for one second; the after screenshot shows the playable corridor, but no current distance/HUD change was captured.
gameplay.outcome: The title transitioned into a rendered corridor with the player character. Current movement response was not confirmed; a separate dated gameplay receipt recorded the distance marker changing from 24 m to 21 m after walking and the blade visibly raising after Swing.
gameplay.limitations: The current pass did not confirm movement, a hit, or an enemy outcome; prior action outcomes are labeled separately.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: The title opened to a rendered 3D corridor after Space; the page lists walk, block, swing, throw-blade, and grip controls.
Prior play confirmed Up moved the data-card distance 24 m to 21 m, Swing raised the blade, and the corridor reset after a later encounter.

rationale: Action is the accurate existing category: the main loop is real-time corridor traversal and blade combat. A health meter alone does not establish Survival, and no supported human multiplayer mode was found.

title: Rise & Raid
mechanics: A medieval village-building game: expand an economy, spend resources on structures, raise an army, and raid other settlements. A 15-step tutorial teaches building and resource management.

actions: Opened the direct page; an initial browser-check response cleared to the game's guest/sign-in landing screen after a short wait.
Inspected the visible Play as guest and Sign in choices; did not sign in or start/save a guest village.
gameplay.outcome: The live landing screen states Build your village, Raise your army, Raid the world. Current play did not advance past the guest-start page; a prior dated receipt confirms a Gold Mine build advanced the tutorial and reduced crystal from 1,000 to 932.
gameplay.limitations: No guest village was created in the current pass; no sign-in was attempted. The detailed construction result is prior gameplay evidence.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: The current game landing screen offers Play as guest or Google sign-in and describes village building, army raising, and raiding; a short browser-check interstitial cleared to this screen.
A prior tester used the guest path, built a Gold Mine through the tutorial, saw step 2/15, and observed crystal decrease from 1,000 to 932.

rationale: Strategy is primary: building structures, allocating resources, and raising an army to raid are planning and resource decisions. The available text does not establish that raid targets are human-controlled, so Multiplayer is not added.
accessIssue: The first response showed a 403 browser-check interstitial; it cleared to the guest landing screen after a short wait.

title: Sadie & Luna
mechanics: A two-dog puzzle-adventure collection. In Find the Way Home, Luna hops and lights dark areas while Sadie shoves obstacles; both dogs must reach the porch. The current level shows a fence, three hearts, and Left/Right/Bark/Play Sadie controls. Other listed modes are a framing/photo challenge and a timed toy-room challenge.

actions: Selected Find the way home and Start from the live game menu.
The level showed Playing Luna, three hearts, the porch objective, and a fenced side-view scene; pressed D once, with no clear current position/objective change captured.
gameplay.outcome: The current page entered the active two-dog level and displayed its objective and controls. A dated prior receipt confirms D moved toward a fence and Hop advanced the objective toward the porch; current movement was not independently verified.
gameplay.limitations: No fence crossing, switch to Sadie, or porch completion was confirmed in the current pass. The live screenshot shows one playable mode, not the full collection's ending.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: Current menu describes Luna hopping/lighting, Sadie shoving, and a two-block home goal; the selected level shows the porch objective and side-view controls.
A prior tester selected Find the way home, moved to a fence with D, used Hop, and advanced the objective toward the porch.

rationale: Puzzle is primary because the dogs have complementary abilities for solving obstacles; Adventure describes the journey home. Platforming traversal and jumping are substantial but lack an existing category, so Platformer is proposed as a shared category. The Play Sadie button is a character switch, not proof of two human players.

title: Ski Jumping
mechanics: A 3D ski-jumping sports game with Training and World Cup modes. Training lets players choose the hill, wind, start gate, suit, and skis before a jump. The current menu explicitly offers creating a tournament with friends.

actions: Opened the live game and selected Training; the current screen showed Lake Placid, hill/wind/start-gate/suit/ski settings and a Jump control.
Attempted the visible Jump control, but the follow-up control lookup timed out before a post-jump screenshot was captured.
gameplay.outcome: The live menu confirms training configuration and a World Cup tournament with friends. A prior dated receipt observed the skier leave the gate and speed rise from 0 to 62.2 km/h; this pass did not capture a jump result.
gameplay.limitations: No landing distance, score, or tournament participant list was observed in this pass; prior jump evidence is separate.

sources.kind: live page, visible controls, or current access check
sources.detail: Current menu offers Training and 'World Cup — Create a tournament with friends'; Training exposes hill, wind, gate, suit, and ski choices before Jump.
A prior tester opened Training, clicked Jump, left the gate, and observed speed increase from 0 to 62.2 km/h.

rationale: Sports is primary because the activity follows ski-jumping rules and technique. The current menu explicitly supports tournaments with friends, which is evidence for human Multiplayer; no race or leaderboard is used to infer that category.
